title: Black holes
examples: How do black holes actually form in space?
What happens if you get too close to a black hole?
Is gravity the only thing that affects black holes?

explain.say: Gravity is the force that pulls objects with mass together.
Black holes have gravity so incredibly strong nothing can escape.
The event horizon is the point of no return around a black hole.

draw.text: Event Horizon: Point of no return

explain.say: If you cross the event horizon, you would fall towards the center.
A concrete example is the Sun's gravity compared to a black hole.
In everyday life, the ocean tide shows us gravity's pull.

faq.q: What is the difference between a black hole and a neutron star?
faq.a: A neutron star is very dense but its gravity is not strong enough to trap light. Black holes have gravity so strong that even light cannot escape.
asks: Are all super-dense stars black holes?
What makes a black hole different from a normal star?

faq.q: Can we actually see black holes if they trap all light?
faq.a: We cannot see the black hole itself because it absorbs all light. However, we can see the effects of its gravity on nearby stars and gas.
asks: How do astronomers detect black holes?
Do black holes glow in any way?

faq.q: What is the singularity at the center of a black hole?
faq.a: The singularity is the theoretical point of infinite density at the very center of the black hole. It is where all the mass is thought to be compressed.
asks: What is inside a black hole?
Is the singularity a physical object?

faq.q: Does gravity affect us on Earth the same way it affects space?
faq.a: Yes, gravity is the fundamental force pulling objects with mass toward each other. On Earth, this pull keeps us grounded.
asks: What is the source of Earth's gravity?

faq.q: If we got near an event horizon, what would happen to us?
faq.a: The tidal forces would stretch us apart in a process called spaghettification. We would be pulled much harder in different directions.
asks: Would we feel anything crossing the horizon?

facts: Black holes are regions in space with extremely strong gravity.
The event horizon marks the boundary from which nothing can escape.
Gravity is the force that pulls objects with mass together.
The singularity is the predicted center of a black hole.

quiz.say: If gravity is stronger than the escape velocity, what happens to light?

options.show: It slows down to a crawl
options.say: It slows down to a crawl

quiz.why: The gravity is so strong that even light, which moves very fast, cannot overcome the pull.

wrong.0: Reflection requires an outward force, which the black hole's gravity overcomes.
wrong.2: This is tempting because slowing down suggests resistance, but the pull is absolute.
wrong.3: This describes gravitational lensing, but the question asks what happens to escape.

options.show: The visible edge of the hole
options.say: The visible edge of the hole

quiz.why: It is the boundary around the black hole where escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.

wrong.1: The singularity is the center, not the boundary itself.
wrong.2: Black holes are invisible; the horizon is an abstract boundary.
wrong.3: Gravity does not stop; it becomes overwhelmingly strong.

quiz.say: If the Sun suddenly became a black hole, what would happen to Earth?

options.show: Earth would fly away into space
options.say: Earth would fly away into space

options.show: Earth would immediately crash into the center
options.say: Earth would immediately crash into the center

options.show: The Earth would get much colder
options.say: The Earth would get much colder

quiz.why: The gravity that holds Earth in orbit is determined by the mass, not the light it emits.

wrong.0: This assumes the loss of gravity, but the mass remains, keeping the orbit.
wrong.1: The orbit is maintained by the gravitational pull, not by the star's light.
wrong.2: While heat would stop, the orbital mechanics are governed by mass, not just energy.
